cases.note: seq would write about 900 MB. A program reads its input as it arrives, as from a pipe, so one that reads a line, or none, ends at once and its writer stops; one that took its input whole first would take seconds and gigabytes.
The input is over 1 MiB, so a backend that serves ranges hands it over in pieces. Monty has no sys.stdin: its input arrives whole, as the stdin global.

command.python:
python3 -c "try:
    data = stdin
except NameError:
    import sys
    data = sys.stdin.buffer.read()
print(len(data), data.count(b'\n'))" < /data/in.txt
command.js:
node -e "const data = new Uint8Array(std.in.readAsArrayBuffer())
console.log(data.length, data.filter((b) => b === 10).length)" < /data/in.txt

command.python:
python3 -c "import sys
n = 0
for line in sys.stdin:
    n += 1
print(n, line, end='')" < /data/in.txt

cat /data/in.txt | python3 -c "import sys
n = 0
for line in sys.stdin:
    n += 1
print(n, line, end='')"
